title: Radiation Storm
short: A solar flare sends a wave of protons your way. You have minutes to take cover.
briefing: A routine day on the station, until space weather turns. When a solar particle event hits, the storm shelter (crew quarters lined with water and equipment) cuts your dose sharply. Get there in time and stay there.

story.intro: The Sun throws a flare at the station. The storm watch from Day 27 just became a warning.
story.goal: Reach the shelter in time and keep your total dose low.

crew.text: All crew: flare confirmed. The shelter is behind the far hatch. Move with purpose.
Dosimeters are climbing in the lab. I've shut the experiments down.
Log your dose when this passes. The flight surgeon will want every number.

carry.goodText: You're rested, and it shows: steady hands, steady pulse.
carry.badText: You're still short on sleep: your heart is already racing.

events.text: Routine day on the station. Space weather is quiet.
Space weather alert: a large solar flare has just erupted. Protons expected in about 10 minutes.
First protons arriving. The dose rate is rising.
Storm peak: the dose rate is hundreds of times normal.
The dose rate is back to normal.

decisions.title: Protons in about 8 minutes
decisions.prompt: Mission Control confirms a solar particle event. What do you do?

choices.label: Go to the storm shelter now
choices.feedback: Water bags and equipment around the crew quarters block much of the proton flux.

choices.label: Finish the experiment first
choices.feedback: Protons arrive close to light speed. Every minute outside the shelter at the peak adds dose. Click the hatch to take cover.

choices.label: Put on extra layers of clothing
choices.feedback: Fabric barely slows high-energy protons. Mass, like water, is what protects you. Click the hatch to take cover.

decisions.title: Stay or go?
decisions.prompt: A crewmate wants you both to leave the shelter for 10 minutes to save an experiment.

choices.label: Stay sheltered until the dose rate is green
choices.feedback: Right. Experiments can be repeated; dose can't be taken back.

choices.label: Go together, quickly
choices.feedback: You're out in the storm peak. Get back in through the hatch.

choices.label: Ask Mission Control first
choices.feedback: Good instinct, and the answer is: stay put while it's red.

decisions.title: Storm over
decisions.prompt: The dose rate is back to normal.

choices.label: Record your dose and report it to the flight surgeon
choices.feedback: Every storm dose goes on your lifetime record, which limits future missions.

choices.label: Nothing to report, the storm has passed
choices.feedback: Dose adds up over a career. It has to be on the record.

actions.label: Move into the storm shelter
actions.message: Hatch closed behind you. Shielding up.

actions.label: Leave the storm shelter
actions.message: Out of the shelter. Only leave once the dose rate is green.

keySteps.label: Get into the storm shelter before the protons arrive
keySteps.why: The first 10 minutes after the warning are all the time you get. Shelter cuts the dose by around 90 %.

successText: Storm over. Your extra dose stayed low.
failText: Too long unprotected at the storm peak. The flight surgeon ordered an emergency review.
